title: She was doing nothing.
paragraphs: She was doing nothing.
At least that’s how it looked.

Martha was moving. Serving. Sweating. Carrying the weight of the room.
Mary was sitting.
And Jesus defended the one who looked less productive.

“Mary… sat at the Lord’s feet and listened to His teaching.”
— Luke 10:39
That verse cut me deep.
Because I’ve been Martha more times than I want to admit.

Busy for God.
Working for God.
Serving around Jesus…
but not slowing down to be with Jesus.

And that is the lesson that humbled me:
Activity is not always intimacy.
You can fill the house with service and still leave your soul empty.
You can prepare meals, organize ministry, help everyone else—
and still miss the voice of the One you claim to love.
But here’s what we miss…

Jesus never rebuked Martha for serving.
He rebuked her for being worried and distracted.

That means the real danger is not work.
It is work that pulls your heart away from worship.
It is service without stillness.
Ministry without presence.
Hands full.
Heart far.

Mary chose the better portion not because she was lazy—
but because she understood something eternal:
Before we do anything for Christ, we must first learn to sit at His feet.

That’s where strength is born.
That’s where peace returns.
That’s where your soul stops performing and starts receiving.

Some of us are exhausted not because we are doing too much,
but because we are doing much without drinking deeply from Jesus.

Sit first.
Listen first.
Love Him first.
Then serve from fullness, not frenzy.

And here’s the Gospel:
Jesus is not looking for frantic performance.
He is calling for surrendered presence.
He didn’t die and rise again just to make you useful.
He saved you so you could know Him, walk with Him, and be transformed by Him.

So today, don’t just ask,
“What do I need to do?”
Ask,
“Have I been with Him?”

Because the better portion is still available.
And His name is Jesus.
